chunks: ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār narrated from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, who said:

I instructed a man to ask Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who takes funds for a hajj from one man, but it does not suffice him. Is it permissible for him to take another hajj fund from another man so that he may have enough by it, and it would suffice on behalf of them both together? Or should he leave them both together if one of them does not suffice him?
Then he mentioned that he said: “It is more beloved to me that it be exclusively for one person; and if it does not suffice him, then he should not take it.”

key_terms.أُخْرَى: another, meaning a second hajj payment from a different person
key_terms.حِجَّةً: funds or commission for performing a hajj on behalf of someone
key_terms.خَالِصَةً: exclusive and devoted solely to one person
key_terms.فَتُجْزِيَ: so that it would validly suffice and discharge the obligation
key_terms.فَلَا تَكْفِيهِ: it does not suffice him or cover the needed expense
key_terms.فَلَا يَأْخُذْهَا: then he should not accept it

ai.seo_question: Can someone combine two separate hajj payments from different people if one payment alone is not enough?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding accepting compensation to perform hajj on behalf of another person when the allotted amount is insufficient. The Imam عليه السلام prefers that the hajj be devoted exclusively to one person, and if the amount does not cover the cost, it should not be accepted.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2926 - Ali ibn Mahziyar narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, who said:

I instructed someone to ask Abu al-Hasan (as) about a man who accepts funds for Hajj from one person, but it is insufficient. Can he then take another Hajj fund from a different person to cover the costs, allowing it to suffice for both of them? Or should he abandon both if one is insufficient?
Imam (as) replied: "It is preferable to dedicate the Hajj exclusively to one person. If it is insufficient, he should not accept it."
